channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Food & Agriculture
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] France expects EU sanctions on 14 December over Iran’s sabotage of supermarket refrigeration, as Iran-linked hackers turn to physical attacks
item.category: Top Story
item.description: France’s foreign minister said on 17 November he expects EU foreign ministers to agree sanctions on 14 December against those behind October’s sabotage of supermarket refrigeration controllers, a day after EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas confirmed new Iran sanctions are being prepared. Paris blames the IRGC’s Shahid Kaveh unit for the attack on about 700 French sites, which French authorities say caused at least 15 fires, and has sought arrest warrants for three officers; Iran rejects the accusations. Health-ISAC warned on 16 November that settings were also changed at French blood-service sites. US and Israeli officials told the Wall Street Journal that Iran-linked hackers also sabotaged equipment at small Midwest water stations and aboard two tankers. For grocers, cold stores and food processors, a state-backed actor has shown it will spoil food stock by remote control (editorial assessment). - Arab News, from AFP (17 Nov 2026, Barrot: EU decision expected 14 Dec); APA (18 Nov 2026, Barrot on France 5: sanctions within a month); dpa, via Yahoo News (16 Nov 2026, Kallas: EU sanctions in preparation); Asharq Al-Awsat and The New Arab (16 Nov 2026, French sanctions push); Health-ISAC (16 Nov 2026, cold-chain bulletin); Wall Street Journal (13 Nov 2026), via Newsmax wire on Yahoo News and Voice of Emirates; RFI via AOL (11 Nov 2026, Paris prosecutor’s warrant request); The Record (9 Nov 2026, French attribution and at least 15 fires); Insurance Journal, from Reuters (13 Nov 2026, BSI warning); Bytes Europe (13 Nov 2026, CCB warning); Midnight Blue (Nov 2026, AK-SM 800A research); GBHackers (13 Nov 2026); NPR (9 Nov 2026, Iranian denial); Iran International (14 Nov 2026, IRGC response); Arab News, from AFP (12 Nov 2026, Belgian statement) - Barrot: EU sanctions within a month 17–18 Nov 2026; EU confirms sanctions in preparation, French sanctions push and Health-ISAC bulletin 16 Nov 2026; WSJ report 13 Nov 2026; BSI and CCB warnings 13 Nov 2026; warrant request 11 Nov 2026; French attribution 9 Nov 2026; IRGC rejects French findings 14 Nov 2026; October attack 11–12 Oct 2026; investigations ongoing

item.title: [Critical] CISA and FBI warn of an ongoing threat to internet-connected refrigeration as European supermarket attacks reach at least 11 countries
item.category: Incident — CISA/FBI/HHS/USDA/DOT joint warning (5 Nov 2026) and a second wave of refrigeration attacks across about 11 European countries (1–4 Nov); Belgium says its evidence points to Iran (12 Nov), no formal attribution
item.description: On 5 November CISA and the FBI, with HHS, USDA and DOT, warned that hackers tampering with internet-connected refrigeration controllers pose an ongoing threat that also reaches cold-storage, healthcare, chemical and transport operations. After hundreds of French stores were hit in October, a second wave on 1–2 November reached about 11 European countries, forcing units into continuous heating or defrost. Sweden’s NCSC says Coop and ICA victims mainly ran older systems from one manufacturer with weak passwords. Belgium’s interior minister said on 12 November that evidence points to Iran, short of formal attribution; a pro-Russian claim is unverified. Exposed Danfoss StoreView instances fell from 3,004 to 708 by 5 November, and Sekoia says the second wave used a non-public flaw that renames the controller’s admin account. Any reachable controller is at risk today (editorial assessment). - TechCrunch (5 Nov 2026, CISA/FBI joint statement); SentinelOne Labs (3 Nov 2026, updated 4 Nov); Cybersecurity Dive (3 Nov 2026, updated with 4 Nov developments); Unit 42 (6 Nov 2026, exposure counts); Censys (6 Nov 2026, exposure analysis); BleepingComputer (5 Nov 2026); Nextgov (29 Oct 2026); Al Jazeera (4 Nov 2026); CERT-FR CERTFR-2026-ALE-012; The Cyber Express (6 Nov 2026, CISA/FBI/HHS/USDA/DOT advisory summary); Industrial Cyber (6 Nov 2026); Help Net Security (6 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (6 Nov 2026, hardening guidance); The Hacker News (9 Nov 2026, exposure trend); eBuilder Security (11 Nov 2026, Swedish government and NCSC warning); Arab News/AFP (12 Nov 2026, Belgian statement); Sekoia TDR (10 Nov 2026, second-wave technique) - Attacks overnight 1–2 Nov 2026; Germany, Romania and UK confirmed 4 Nov 2026; CISA/FBI joint warning 5 Nov 2026; French attribution of the October attack 9 Nov 2026; Swedish government warning 10 Nov 2026; Belgian minister points to Iran 12 Nov 2026 — investigations ongoing

item.title: [High] A security breach keeps USDA payment, loan and mapping systems offline for farmers for most of a week
item.category: Incident — Security incident at the US Department of Agriculture; applications offline since about 16 Nov 2026 after a department-wide password reset; officially acknowledged 20 Nov 2026; IT systems only; no attribution
item.description: The US Department of Agriculture has kept many applications offline since about 16 November after its security operations centre found an intrusion, including payment, loan and mapping tools that farmers and field staff use. An internal email reported by Nextgov says IT staff reset every database password across all environments, which caused the outages. On 20 November Under Secretary Richard Fordyce called it a cyberthreat, said no personal information was involved and no data was lost, and expected most systems back within days. Former officials quoted by NBC News say data theft has not been ruled out. No attacker has been named and nothing points to OT. Food and agriculture operators should plan for agency systems they depend on being unavailable for a week (editorial assessment). - Nextgov/FCW (19 Nov 2026, internal email and password reset); ABC News, citing DTN (20 Nov 2026, Fordyce remarks; Iowa Farmers Union); IBTimes UK, citing NBC News (21 Nov 2026, affected systems and former officials) - Outages from about 16 Nov 2026; USDA acknowledged a cyberthreat 20 Nov 2026; restoration ongoing

item.title: [High] The Pentagon still will not say whether August commissary freezer failures were a cyberattack, as Army investigators work with French police
item.category: Suspected incident — Refrigeration failures at US military commissaries (on-base grocery stores), late August 2026; investigators suspect a cyberattack; cause still not confirmed as of 4 Nov 2026
item.description: Investigators are still treating late-August refrigeration failures at no fewer than six US military commissaries, the on-base grocery stores, as a suspected cyberattack, with no cause confirmed. Reuters reported on 29 October, citing unnamed officials, that refrigerators and freezers switched to defrost and warmed, spoiling food at bases including Fort Huachuca and Fort Irwin, and that US Cyber Command has joined Army and Air Force inquiries. Stars and Stripes reported on 4 November that the Army CID cyber field office is working with the Defense Criminal Investigative Service and with French law enforcement on the October attacks in France; the Pentagon still declines to say whether a cyberattack occurred or how many stores were hit. Nextgov/FCW sources suspect Iran-linked hackers; no agency has attributed it. The forced-defrost pattern matches France, but this remains unconfirmed (editorial assessment). - Stars and Stripes (4 Nov 2026, Army CID, DCIS and French law enforcement); Reuters (29 Oct 2026), via The Next Web; Nextgov/FCW (29 Oct 2026); Military Times (28 Aug 2026); Stars and Stripes (1 and 30 Sep 2026) - Failures in late August 2026; reported as a suspected cyberattack 29 Oct 2026; investigation update 4 Nov 2026 — cause not confirmed

item.title: [Critical] Attackers rooted unpatched Check Point gateways through PHP2Shell, planted backdoors and wiped a VMware host; the root flaw is now in KEV
item.category: Incident — PHP2Shell plus Gaia root flaw CVE-2026-123039 used to backdoor Check Point gateways and wipe a VMware ESXi host (wave 1 from 30 Oct, Israel; wave 2 from 2 Nov, multiple countries); CVE-2026-123039 added to CISA KEV 13 Nov 2026
item.description: Check Point Research said on 12 November that attackers exploited the PHP2Shell flaws on unpatched Check Point Mobile Access portals from 30 October, then used a local flaw (CVE-2026-123039) to become root. They planted backdoors, pivoted to a VMware ESXi host and ran a wiper. The first wave hit Israeli organizations, some destructively; a second wave from 2 November reached several countries without destruction. Attribution is unconfirmed (tooling resembles China-nexus UNC5221). CISA added the root flaw to KEV on 13 November. No OT victim is reported, but these firewalls often sit at the IT/OT boundary and ESXi often hosts HMIs and historians (editorial assessment). - Check Point Research (12 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (13 Nov 2026); Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AV26-1154 (12 Nov 2026, updated 13 Nov); CISA KEV alert (13 Nov 2026); BleepingComputer (Nov 2026) - Wave 1 from 30 Oct 2026; wave 2 from 2 Nov 2026; research published 12 Nov 2026; KEV addition 13 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Cyberattack on Brazil’s Santos port authority forces manual workarounds at Latin America’s busiest port
item.category: Incident — Cyberattack on the Santos Port Authority (APS), Brazil; systems down from 6 Nov 2026, attack confirmed 10 Nov; port security raised to level 2 of 3 (8 Nov); core systems in final tests 16 Nov 2026; about 70% of backups recovered; Federal Police inquiry opened 10 Nov; no attribution
item.description: The Port of Santos authority, which runs Brazil’s largest port, lost its IT systems on 6 November and on 10 November confirmed a cyberattack. Access-control systems and digital tools for coordinating port operations went down, delaying vessel, truck and train procedures and forcing some checks, such as matching ship dimensions to berths, to be done by hand. The port’s protection level was raised to 2 of 3 on 8 November. By 16 November main internal systems were in final tests and about 70% of affected file backups were recovered; ship movements and landside access continued throughout. Brazil’s Federal Police are investigating; the attacker, entry route and any data theft are undisclosed. Santos is a major outlet for Brazilian agricultural exports such as sugar, soy and coffee, so food and ag shippers should confirm their forwarders’ manual fallbacks (editorial assessment). - The Rio Times (16 Nov 2026, status update citing the Santos Port Authority); DatamarNews (10 Nov 2026, updated 11 Nov, citing A Tribuna); CyberDelegate (17 Nov 2026, citing Folha de S.Paulo, CNN Brasil and Agência Brasil); Interlira Reports (17 Nov 2026) - Outage from 6 Nov 2026; security level raised 8 Nov 2026; attack confirmed 10 Nov 2026; core systems in final tests and ~70% of backups recovered 16–17 Nov 2026; investigation ongoing

item.title: [Critical] PHP2Shell attacks rooted about two dozen Palo Alto firewalls, and Siemens, Schneider and ABB now list grid-control, DCS and RTU products, several with no fix
item.category: Active exploitation — PHP2Shell chained with a Linux kernel flaw to root exposed PAN-OS firewalls, 23–24 Oct; OT vendor advisories 28–30 Oct; Siemens adds metering gateways 16 Nov
item.description: Palo Alto’s Unit 42 verified that a suspected China-nexus actor chained the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) with Linux kernel bug CVE-2026-46300 to root about two dozen internet-exposed PAN-OS firewalls on 23–24 October and steal Active Directory credentials. Siemens (Spectrum Power, AMIS TS and, since 16 November, WTV676/WTV776 metering gateways), Schneider (a Foxboro DCS server) and ABB (Netcontrol RTUs, ASPECT gateways) now list affected products, several unfixed. None is reported exploited and no OT operator is named: treat it as an IT-to-OT boundary warning. - Unit 42 (updated 29 Oct 2026); Palo Alto Networks advisory for CVE-2026-109618 (updated 29 Oct 2026); The Record (29 Oct 2026) and Infosecurity Magazine (30 Oct 2026), citing Dream; CISA KEV catalog (30 Oct 2026 release); Siemens SSA-166980 V1.4 (16 Nov 2026, WTV676/WTV776 added; V1.2 29 Oct 2026), SSA-566512 V1.1 (28 Oct 2026), SSA-019113 and SSA-082556; Schneider Electric SESB-2026-295-01 v3.2.0 (30 Oct 2026); ABB Netcontrol and Arctic advisories (30 Oct 2026), ASPECT advisory (29 Oct 2026) and APROL SA26P015 (23 Oct 2026); CERT@VDE VDE-2026-127 and VDE-2026-137 - Root compromises 23–24 Oct 2026, verified by Unit 42 29 Oct 2026; KEV additions 26 and 28 Oct 2026; Siemens, Schneider and ABB updates 28–30 Oct 2026; Siemens metering gateways added 16 Nov 2026

item.title: [Medium] Dragos counts 1,266 ransomware attacks on industrial organizations in Q3, up 11%, and found no case of an operator touching a control system
item.category: Research — Dragos Industrial Ransomware Analysis for Q3 2026 (published 16 Nov 2026), covering July–September; Check Point October 2026 statistics (12 Nov 2026) for comparison
item.description: Dragos said on 16 November that ransomware hit 1,266 industrial organizations between July and September 2026, up 11% on the second quarter, while the number of brands claiming industrial victims jumped from 70 to 99. Manufacturing took 69% of cases, followed by the ICS ecosystem of integrators, engineering firms and equipment makers (116) and transport and logistics (105); oil and gas logged 47. Qilin and The Gentlemen drove 29% of the total. Dragos saw no Q3 case of a ransomware operator manipulating a control system: production stopped because the IT, ERP and virtualization layers plants rely on went down, as when Fairlife reportedly halted all four of its US plants for about 11 days. Entry came through edge devices and enterprise applications exploited within days of disclosure, and through stolen VPN and firewall credentials. Check Point separately counted a record 1,063 claimed victims across all sectors in October. - Dragos (16 Nov 2026); Australian Cyber Security Magazine (17 Nov 2026); Check Point Research October 2026 statistics, via iTWire (12 Nov 2026) - Published 16 Nov 2026; data covers July–September 2026

item.title: [Medium] DHS tells Congress Iran-backed hackers have stepped up attacks on US water, energy and transport since February, while officials rule out hacking in last week’s outages
item.category: Government threat assessment — DHS Secretary’s written testimony to the House Homeland Security Committee (18 Nov 2026); DNI and DHS tell the same hearing recent US outages were not cyberattacks
item.description: In written testimony for a House Homeland Security Committee hearing on 18 November, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Iranian state-sponsored groups and pro-Iranian criminals have targeted US critical infrastructure since the conflict with Iran began in February, with transportation, healthcare, water, energy and financial services increasingly in their sights. He described the attacks so far as mostly localized, low-damage disruptions of poorly secured industrial control systems, but warned that weak systems and poor cyber hygiene could have devastating consequences. At the same hearing the Director of National Intelligence and DHS said they found no evidence that hackers caused last week’s Microsoft 365 outage, the nationwide FAA ground stop or other recent disruptions, which officials tie to software defects and upgrade failures. Separately, AttackIQ research released on 17 November describes Iranian groups handing network access to one another, with long-running espionage access later passed to teams pursuing destructive goals, sometimes disguised as ransomware or hacktivism, often reaching targets through contractors and suppliers. For OT owners, the official US view now matches France’s: Iran is going after the weakest exposed controllers. - Jerusalem Post (18 Nov 2026, Mullin written testimony); Report.az (18 Nov 2026); Bloomberg (18 Nov 2026); Federal News Network (18 Nov 2026, outages not a coordinated attack); Washington Examiner (18 Nov 2026, hearing); AttackIQ “Weighing Cyber Power”, via Water Online (17 Nov 2026) - Testimony and hearing 18 Nov 2026; AttackIQ research 17 Nov 2026

item.title: [Medium] Bloomberg: Russia-aligned hacktivists have tampered with exposed controls since 2024, including at a Los Angeles-area meatpacker and two Spanish wineries
item.category: Research — Review of Russia-aligned hacktivist tampering with internet-exposed controls (Bloomberg, 27 Oct); food cases from 2024–2026; who carried out or confirmed each case is mostly not stated
item.description: Bloomberg News published a review on 27 October of a loose network of hackers sympathetic to Russia that it says has carried out hundreds of attacks on water treatment plants, factories, dams and other sensitive sites in countries seen as hostile to Russia. The cases date from 2024 to this summer, and two touch food directly. Bloomberg reports that heating and ventilation systems at two Spanish wineries sent temperatures spiking in production and storage areas, and, according to Meduza’s summary of the paywalled article, that a meatpacking plant near Los Angeles had its refrigeration shut off in 2024, spoiling meat, followed by an ammonia leak that forced an evacuation. Who carried out or confirmed those food cases is not stated. The strongest confirmed case in the review is a water one: Denmark’s Defence Intelligence Service attributed the December 2024 attack on the Tureby Alkestrup waterworks, which burst pipes and cut water to about 50 households for seven hours and about 450 for one hour, to the pro-Russian group Z-Pentest. The review covers groups including CARR and Z-Pentest; their own claims of further attacks are not independently verified. Editorial assessment: these attacks need no malware, only a remotely reachable controller with a weak password, which makes exposed refrigeration, HVAC and ammonia-plant controls in food facilities an easy target. - Bloomberg News via Bloomberg Law (27 Oct; partly paywalled); Meduza summary (28 Oct); Danish Defence Intelligence Service attribution via Euronews and AP/SecurityWeek (Dec 2025) - Review published 27 Oct 2026; cases from 2024 to summer 2026

item.title: [Medium] Claroty finds 65,000 game consoles, smart speakers and cars on critical-infrastructure networks, most of them on production segments
item.category: Research — Claroty analysis of 45 million devices at 30,000+ critical-infrastructure sites (released 17 Nov 2026); cross-sector, carried for food and agriculture as editorial assessment; no CVE IDs published
item.description: Claroty said on 17 November that, across 45 million devices at more than 30,000 critical-infrastructure sites, it found about 65,000 consumer gadgets that do not belong on operational networks: game consoles, smart-home and entertainment devices, and connected cars. Industrial sites held 963 game consoles, nearly 90% of them on production rather than guest networks, and thousands of connected vehicles were attached to site networks with almost none isolated on a guest segment. The study does not break out food plants, but processing sites, cold stores and farms with shared Wi-Fi face the same problem. Each unmanaged device is a foothold that quietly undermines the segmentation protecting packaging lines and refrigeration controls (editorial assessment). - Claroty press release, via PR Newswire (17 Nov 2026); Facilities Dive (18 Nov 2026); Help Net Security (19 Nov 2026) - Research released 17 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Hackers probe 14 newly disclosed flaws in end-of-life Copeland XWEB EVO refrigeration controllers, five of which will never be fixed
item.category: Advisory — 14 flaws in end-of-life Copeland (Dixell) XWEB EVO refrigeration supervisors disclosed by VulnCheck; CVE records published 12 Nov 2026 (incl. CVE-2026-124010, CVE-2026-124014); exploitation attempts seen within hours; five flaws will not be fixed
item.description: VulnCheck has disclosed 14 vulnerabilities in Copeland’s XWEB EVO, the Dixell supervisory system that runs supermarket and cold-storage refrigeration, each of which gave its researcher root on test units. Nine affect only firmware built before a 2021 rewrite and include unauthenticated command execution and a hard-coded admin password. The other five reach the latest firmware: the daily admin password is derived from the device’s MAC address and the date, and the MAC address is visible without logging in, so an attacker can compute the password, turn on SSH and log in as root. VulnCheck’s sensors saw exploitation attempts against two older-firmware flaws within two hours of the 12 November CVE publication; it calls the sources opportunistic scanners, not the state campaign in France. Copeland ended XWEB EVO support on 16 March 2026 and will not fix the five current-firmware flaws; nearly 2,000 units are reachable from the internet. CyberScoop adds that XBOW honeypots posing as these controllers drew hundreds of requests and login attempts within a day, and someone changed the temperature on one simulated freezer. - SecurityWeek (16 Nov 2026, VulnCheck research and exploitation telemetry; Copeland end-of-life notice); CyberScoop (13 Nov 2026, XBOW honeypot findings; Copeland statement); CERT-FR CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 - CVE records published 12 Nov 2026; probing 12–13 Nov 2026; reported 16 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Danfoss assigns two critical CVEs to its refrigeration system managers, confirms firmware 5.4.0 is affected, and says the fix will not come until 5.5.x
item.description: Danfoss published two security advisories on 20 November that put CVE numbers on the refrigeration-controller weaknesses behind this month’s European warnings. CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS v4 9.3) is a stack buffer overflow in an unauthenticated web handler of AK-SM 8xxA system managers, the store-level controllers that run supermarket and cold-storage refrigeration, up to and including firmware 5.4.0, which settles the earlier dispute over whether 5.4.0 was safe. Danfoss says the fix will come in the upcoming 5.5.x release, which will also remove the option to switch Strict mode off. CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS v4 9.9) covers default credentials documented in the manuals of legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800 units, all versions. The advisories follow Midnight Blue’s disclosure of six pre-login overflows and warnings from Belgium’s CCB, Germany’s BSI and Ireland’s NCSC. CISA republished the Danfoss advisory for US operators on 24 November as ICSA-26-328-03. Neither CVE is reported as exploited or listed in CISA KEV. Until 5.5.x ships, keeping these units off the internet is the real control. - CISA ICSA-26-328-03 (24 Nov 2026); Danfoss DSA-2026-12-01 and DSA-2026-12-02 (20 Nov 2026), as published in the CVE records (via OpenCVE and CVE Brief); Midnight Blue (Nov 2026); The Hacker News (16 Nov 2026, CCB, BSI and Irish NCSC warnings); Bytes Europe (13 Nov 2026, CCB warning); Insurance Journal, from Reuters (13 Nov 2026, BSI warning) - CISA republication 24 Nov 2026; Danfoss advisories and CVEs 20 Nov 2026; CCB and BSI warnings 13 Nov 2026; research published Nov 2026

item.title: [High] A Brotli flaw already in CISA’s exploited list reaches Siemens BRAUMAT brewery batch control and WinCC; most products have no fix yet
item.category: Advisory — Siemens SSA-242944 (10 Nov 2026), republished by CISA as ICSA-26-321-03 (17 Nov 2026): CVE-2026-111497, Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write, already in CISA KEV since 27 Oct 2026; WinCC, WinCC OA, BRAUMAT/SISTAR and TIA Administrator affected; most products have no fix yet
item.description: Siemens says a widely used compression library flaw, CVE-2026-111497, reaches into several of its industrial software lines, and CISA republished the assessment as an ICS advisory on 17 November. The bug is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder that can crash the software, leak information or possibly allow code execution. CISA added the CVE to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 27 October because of attacks elsewhere; nobody has reported exploitation through a Siemens product. Affected products named include BRAUMAT and SISTAR V8.2, WinCC OA V3.20 and V3.21, WinCC Runtime Professional, WinCC V7/V8 and TIA Administrator. Fixes exist only for BRAUMAT/SISTAR (V8.2 Update 5) and WinCC OA V3.20 (P17.1), so most sites must rely on the workaround for now. BRAUMAT is Siemens’ process control system for breweries and other beverage plants, and WinCC is a common HMI on food lines, which makes this the Siemens advisory most relevant to food and beverage processors (editorial assessment). - CISA ICSA-26-321-03 (17 Nov 2026); Siemens ProductCERT SSA-242944 (10 Nov 2026); CISA KEV alert (27 Oct 2026); Viakoo daily OT briefing via Security Boulevard (22 Nov 2026) - Siemens advisory 10 Nov 2026; CISA republication 17 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] A vCenter authentication bypass was exploited as a zero-day for two months before Broadcom’s 19 November patch; vCenter 7.0 gets no fix
item.category: Active exploitation — VMware vCenter authentication bypass CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS 9.8) exploited as a zero-day for more than two months by a suspected China-linked group, per Mandiant; Broadcom fix released 19 Nov 2026; no public fix for vCenter 7.0
item.description: Broadcom patched CVE-2026-123890 on 19 November, a critical flaw in vCenter’s directory service that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker obtain an administrator session. Google’s Mandiant, which reported the bug, says a suspected China-linked espionage group it tracks as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221, also called Warp Panda) exploited it for more than two months beforehand. In the incidents Mandiant investigated, the group got in through a BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw, moved to Linux appliances, attacked vCenter in early September with a custom tool called Bonesaw, stole SAML signing material and the vCenter master key, created an SSO admin account, forged tokens and moved on to ESXi hosts. Fixes are in vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 and 8.0 U3m; end-of-life vCenter 7.0 has no public patch. No victims or sectors are named. Many plants run HMIs, historians and engineering workstations as virtual machines, so whoever controls vCenter controls those hosts (editorial assessment). - SecurityWeek (19 Nov 2026, citing Broadcom, Google Threat Intelligence/Mandiant and Mandiant CTO Charles Carmakal); CISA KEV alert (20 Nov 2026); The Hacker News (20–21 Nov 2026) - Added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026; patched 19 Nov 2026; exploited from at least early Sep 2026

item.title: [High] Attackers root clustered Cisco Expressway gateways soon after a public exploit, and CISA adds the flaw to KEV
item.category: Active exploitation — Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8), clustered Expressway Core/Edge; exploited after a public PoC (reported by F6); added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026; fixed in X15.5.20
item.description: Security firm F6 says attackers exploited CVE-2026-76466, a critical flaw in clustered Cisco Expressway Core and Edge deployments, shortly after proof-of-concept code appeared on GitHub. They broke into two internet-facing Expressway nodes at an unnamed Russian organization, moved to two more cluster nodes inside the network, and gained root. From there they ran Python scripts, which F6 says show signs of AI-assisted writing, to scan for SMB shares, SQL Server and WinRM hosts and to search GitLab for credentials. CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on 20 November alongside the vCenter zero-day. Cisco disclosed and fixed it on 21 October; there is no workaround. No OT victim is reported, but Expressway is a perimeter gateway that often bridges outside callers into internal networks, so an exposed, unpatched cluster is a foothold close to plant-side systems (editorial assessment). - Security Affairs (21 Nov 2026, CISA KEV additions of 20 Nov); SecurityWeek (Nov 2026, citing F6); Security Affairs (20 Nov 2026, F6 findings) - Added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026; exploitation reported 18–20 Nov 2026; patched 21 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] N-able ships Hotfix 3 for 17 more N-central flaws after attackers planted miners on servers already running Hotfix 2
item.category: Active exploitation — N-able N-central: 4EverAble2Shell exploited to plant miners (13 Nov 2026); N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 fixes 17 more CVEs and removes the Legacy API (16–17 Nov 2026); separate breach of N-able’s hosted Mail Assure/SpamExperts cloud disclosed 20 Nov 2026
item.description: N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 on 16 November, which it calls a critical security update. It fixes 17 new CVEs, including authentication bypasses, missing authorization checks, path traversal leading to code execution and a syslog injection that runs commands as root, and it removes the Legacy API option that the actively exploited 4EverAble2Shell chain depends on. On-premises servers need the upgrade now; hosted servers update automatically, but every customer must also upgrade Agents and Probes, which N-able warns can otherwise be impersonated. The fix follows Huntback’s 13 November finding of cryptocurrency miners on 21 N-central servers, 19 of them on Hotfix 2. Remote control and Intune integration stay blocked for now. Separately, N-able said on 20 November that attackers reached a server in its hosted Mail Assure and SpamExperts email-filtering cloud, forcing it to take the management portal and APIs offline; it says mail flow continued, it has found no access to customer data, and the breach is unrelated to N-central. Many integrators manage plant-side Windows hosts through RMM tools, and a miner today can be a hands-on intruder tomorrow (editorial assessment). - BleepingComputer (20 Nov 2026, Mail Assure/SpamExperts breach); The Hacker News (17 Nov 2026, Hotfix 3, citing N-able release notes of 16 Nov); The Hacker News (13 Nov 2026, citing Huntback and Previdian); The Hacker News (12 Nov 2026, new chains); SecurityWeek (13 Nov 2026); Tenable (10 Nov 2026) - Mail Assure breach disclosed 20 Nov 2026; Hotfix 3 released 16 Nov 2026; exploitation reported 13 Nov 2026; Able2Shell disclosed 9 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Java4Shell exploitation attempts begin, and Siemens tells customers to take Industrial Edge Management offline until patched
item.category: Advisory — OpenJDK “Java4Shell” memory-corruption flaw CVE-2026-114938 (disclosed and patched 17 Nov 2026); exploitation attempts seen 18–19 Nov 2026; Siemens SSA-272816 lists three Industrial Edge Management products
item.description: Probing for Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a memory-corruption bug in how OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later decode Base64 data, started within two days of its 17 November disclosure. GreyNoise counted more than 150 matching requests from five addresses by early 19 November and Previdian logged nine attempts from six addresses; none is confirmed to have succeeded. Exploitation needs a recent Intel or AMD x86-64 processor with AVX-512 VBMI, and researchers at Calif showed unauthenticated code execution against default Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and Keycloak setups, each with a tailored chain. For OT teams the key item is Siemens advisory SSA-272816: three Industrial Edge Management products are affected, fixes are in progress, and Siemens recommends taking those instances offline until they are patched. Cisco lists more than a dozen products with no fix yet, and Atlassian Data Center products are also unpatched. - SecurityWeek (19 Nov 2026, citing Calif, GreyNoise, WatchTowr, Cloudflare, Previdian, Siemens SSA-272816, Cisco and Atlassian); The Record (18 Nov 2026, CISA alert) - Disclosed and patched 17 Nov 2026; exploitation attempts 18–19 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] CISA republishes Mitsubishi Electric’s ICONICS advisory: a CVSS 9.1 flaw and a shared unlock code, with no fix coming for MC Works64, GENESIS32 or BizViz
item.category: Advisory — Mitsubishi Electric ICONICS HMI/SCADA suite (CISA ICSA-26-300-02, 27 Oct); no known exploitation; some products will not be fixed
item.description: CISA republished Mitsubishi Electric’s ICONICS advisory 2026-006 (vendor date 15 October) as ICSA-26-300-02 on 27 October. It covers GENESIS 11.03 and earlier; GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI and IoTWorX 10.97.3 and earlier; and every version of MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz. The most serious flaw, CVE-2026-16438 (CVSS v3.1 9.1 in the advisory), is an incorrect privilege assignment that the advisory says allows arbitrary operations. CVE-2026-16436 (8.1) lets a remote attacker unlock the system with a challenge response that is fixed and the same for every user, CVE-2026-16437 (6.4) lets a local administrator tamper with the file that stores it, and the bundled libwebp flaw CVE-2023-4863 (CVSS v3.1 8.2 in the advisory) can run code if an administrator imports a crafted file. The fixes are GENESIS 11.04 and version 10.98 of the GENESIS64 family (10.97.3 already fixes the libwebp flaw). Mitsubishi plans no fix for MC Works64, GENESIS32 or BizViz and recommends replacing them with GENESIS64 or GENESIS; until then it advises swapping the challenge-response file for a blank one with write access locked down, letting only administrators log in and blocking remote logins from untrusted networks. No exploitation of ICONICS products is reported; the libwebp flaw has been in CISA’s KEV catalog since 13 September 2023 because of browser exploitation. Editorial assessment: GENESIS64 and Hyper Historian are used for HMI, historian and energy monitoring in many process plants, food and beverage among them, and older GENESIS32 installations tend to linger on line PCs. - Mitsubishi Electric PSIRT advisory 2026-006 (primary, 15 Oct); CISA ICSA-26-300-02 via CISA’s CSAF record (27 Oct); CISA KEV entry for CVE-2023-4863 (13 Sep 2023) - Vendor advisory 15 Oct 2026; CISA republication 27 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] Bluetooth flaws let a nearby attacker apply or release trailer brakes on Elecbrakes controllers, and the oldest model is still unpatched
item.category: Advisory — Elecbrakes EB2, VM1 and ELBC 2000 Bluetooth trailer brake controllers (CISA ICSA-26-323-02); two critical flaws; no exploitation reported; cross-sector, carried for agriculture as editorial assessment
item.description: Element Digital researchers found three Bluetooth flaws in Elecbrakes trailer brake controllers (EB2, VM1 and ELBC 2000), two rated critical, covering missing authentication and weak replay protection. An attacker within about 100 metres could engage or release a trailer’s brakes, or change braking force, without the driver doing anything. A third, medium-severity firmware-update flaw is considered theoretical. CISA published advisory ICSA-26-323-02 last week. Elecbrakes shipped firmware for EB2 and VM1 in early July and says about 60–70% of controllers in daily use have it; a fix for the older ELBC 2000 is still in progress. There is no evidence of malicious exploitation. For farms and haulers towing livestock, grain or equipment trailers, this is a road-safety issue on a wireless link, not a plant-network one (editorial assessment). - SecurityWeek (24 Nov 2026, Element Digital research and vendor response); CISA ICSA-26-323-02 (Nov 2026) - Advisory published week of 16 Nov 2026; SecurityWeek report 24 Nov 2026

item.title: [Medium] GAO finds USDA and FDA fall short on cyber threat sharing and emergency exercises for the food and agriculture sector
item.category: Policy — GAO-27-108656, Critical Infrastructure Protection: Further Action Needed to Enhance Cybersecurity of the Food and Agriculture Sector (published 19 Nov 2026); 5 recommendations to USDA and HHS/FDA
item.description: GAO reported on 19 November that USDA and the FDA, the sector’s lead federal agencies, met most cyber-related requirements Congress set in the FY2021 National Defense Authorization Act but only partially met or missed five, mainly on threat-information sharing and emergency preparedness. Both agencies cited a lack of resources and staffing, and ABC News reports they have not run food-sector cyberattack response exercises since 2024. GAO made five recommendations: two to USDA’s Office of Homeland Security and three to the FDA’s Office of Coordinated Outbreak Response, covering information sharing with CISA, preparedness exercises and, for FDA, planning documents for cyber emergencies. HHS agreed; USDA disagreed with its two and asked GAO to remove or redirect them, and GAO kept them. GAO recalls the 2021 ransomware attack on a global meat processor that shut major slaughterhouses. Plan to run your own exercises (editorial assessment). - GAO-27-108656 (19 Nov 2026); ABC News (20 Nov 2026) - Published 19 Nov 2026
